results.title: Orinda Sun 1957-05-03
results.creator: Silverman, Herman, 1920-2011
description: Please visit the California Revealed website to see the most complete and up-to-date version of this object: https://californiarevealed.org/node/528430 .

The Orinda Sun Newspapers focus on the unincorporated town of Orinda, California from 1948 to 1972. During this time period Orinda went from a small rural area to a thriving suburb of the SF Bay area. While the Orinda Sun would occasionally run stories about Contra Costa County, California state or national interest, the focus was on articles of local significance like transportation needs (like BART or Highway 24 freeway), development plans, Orinda community events, and culture of the people who had settled in this area through stories, wanted ads, obituaries, wedding and birth announcements and the many ads for local establishments.

During this time period, Orinda went from being a small rural town to a thriving suburb of the San Francisco Bay area. results.creator: Silverman, Herman, 1920-2011
description: Please visit the California Revealed website to see the most complete and up-to-date version of this object: https://californiarevealed.org/node/534555 .
Cut off text is inherent to the original newspaper. Text loss occurs due to the manner in which the object was bound.

The Orinda Sun newspapers focused on the unincorporated town of Orinda, California from 1948 to 1972. During this time period, Orinda went from being a small rural town to a thriving suburb of the San Francisco Bay area. While the Orinda Sun would occasionally run stories about Contra Costa county and statewide or national interests, the focus was on articles of local significance, such as transportation needs (BART, Highway 24), development plans, Orinda community events, and the culture of the people who settled in this area through their stories, want ads, obituaries, wedding and birth announcements, and the many advertisements for local establishments.
